button.name: Button
button.description: An action. Fill shows how important it is: one ink-filled main action per view, the next outlined, the rest plain.
button.example:
<button class="ds-button ds-button--primary" type="button">Start</button>
<button class="ds-button" type="button">Reset</button>
<button class="ds-button ds-button--ghost" type="button">Cancel</button>
<button class="ds-button" type="button" disabled>Stop</button>

variantGuidance.primary: class="ds-button ds-button--primary": the one main action in a view, ink-filled.

constraints: One primary button per view.
The label is a verb for what it does: Start, Reset, Send. Sentence case.
40 px tall (--ds-control-height); 44 px targets on a phone (--ds-touch).
Corners signal function: this is something you act on, so it takes --ds-radius-act.
Never color a button by status; colors are for status and data only.
A label that changes (Start and Stop, Copy and Copied) holds every label in a .ds-hold, so the button keeps one width and nothing beside it moves.

accessibility.focusVisible: The 2 px ink focus ring with a 2 px offset.
accessibility.disabled: Use the disabled attribute; the button reads as disabled without a color change alone.

validChildren: an inline SVG icon before the text
anatomy.compositionNotes: Put buttons in a row with --ds-space-3 between them; the primary first.

icon-button.name: Icon button
icon-button.description: A small square action shown as an icon alone: home, full screen, present, the light and dark switch.
constraints: Always an aria-label naming the action.
The icon is 16 px, drawn in the current text color.
Square, 32 px (--ds-control-height-sm).
Corners signal function: this is something you act on, so it takes --ds-radius-act.

slots.icon: One inline SVG, 16 px, stroke or fill currentColor, aria-hidden.

anatomy.compositionNotes: In the top bar they sit in .ds-tools, at the right.

theme-toggle.name: Light and dark button
theme-toggle.description: One icon button that shows the theme it switches to: a moon in light, a sun in dark. Kept as ds.theme; with nothing kept, the system's setting rules.
constraints: Load /v2/theme.js.
Put the head script from the top of theme.js in <head>, so a kept choice applies before the page paints.
Never a labeled switch: TJ chose the icon to save space.

ariaRequired: aria-label, which theme.js keeps as "Switch to dark" or "Switch to light"

anatomy.root: <button class="ds-icon-button" type="button" data-ds-theme-toggle aria-label="Switch to dark">
anatomy.compositionNotes: Last in the top bar's tools.

input.name: Input
input.description: A one-line text field. A box means you can type here.
input.example:
<label class="ds-label" for="ex-search">Search</label>
<input class="ds-input" id="ex-search" type="text" placeholder="Model or vocabulary">
<label class="ds-label" for="ex-token-id">Token id</label>
<input class="ds-input ds-input--mono" id="ex-token-id" type="text" inputmode="numeric" value="1820">

variantGuidance.mono: class="ds-input ds-input--mono": for what a model reads or writes, such as a prompt or a token id.

constraints: Every field has a visible label (a .ds-label or text), not a placeholder alone.
Only inputs and menus are boxes; read-only content never is.
Corners signal function: this is something you act on, so it takes --ds-radius-act.

anatomy.compositionNotes: Label above the field, --ds-space-2 between them.

textarea.name: Text area
textarea.example:
<label class="ds-label" for="ex-prompt">Prompt</label>
<textarea class="ds-textarea ds-textarea--mono" id="ex-prompt" rows="3">Once upon a time,</textarea>
constraints: Use the mono variant for a prompt or anything a model reads.
Corners signal function: this is something you act on, so it takes --ds-radius-act.

select.name: Menu
select.description: A choice from a list, marked ▾.
constraints: Wrap it in .ds-select-wrap, which draws the ▾.
Corners signal function: this is something you act on, so it takes --ds-radius-act.

segmented.name: Segmented control
segmented.description: One of a few choices, all in view, such as List | Field.
constraints: Two to four short choices; more goes in a menu.
The chosen one has aria-pressed="true".
Corners signal function: this is something you act on, so it takes --ds-radius-act.

tag.name: Tag
tag.description: A status you read: Raw, Templated, Failed. A word or two in a hairline frame.
tag.example: Vendored Raw Templated Failed
constraints: The word carries the meaning; the color only repeats it. Never color alone.
A tag is read, never clicked; a clickable filter is a chip.
A tag whose word changes (Idle, Running) holds every word in a .ds-hold, so it keeps one width.

accessibility.notes: Its text is the status; no aria needed.

chip.name: Chip
chip.description: A filter you turn on and off.
chip.example:
<button class="ds-chip" type="button" aria-pressed="true">Raw only</button>
<button class="ds-chip" type="button" aria-pressed="false">Vendored tokenizer</button>
constraints: A chip acts; a tag reads.
Pressed is ink; its weight and size never change, so a row of chips holds still.
Corners signal function: this is something you act on, so it takes --ds-radius-act.

anatomy.compositionNotes: A row of chips with --ds-space-2 between.

switch.name: Switch
switch.description: An on/off setting that takes effect at once.
switch.example: Color by token
constraints: Label it with visible text (aria-labelledby).
Not for light and dark, which is the icon button.

hold.name: Held place
hold.description: One place for things that take turns: a button's labels, a tag's words, a Retry button that comes and goes. It is as wide and as tall as the largest thing in it, shown or hidden, so a change moves nothing around it.
hold.example: IdleRunning

variantGuidance.default: class="ds-hold": the shown form starts at the left (centered in a button, a chip or a tag).
variantGuidance.end: class="ds-hold ds-hold--end": for a number, which ends where its widest form would, so its last figure stays put.

constraints: Show one child and hide the rest with the hidden attribute: inside a .ds-hold, a hidden child keeps its space.
Never hide with opacity: 0, which leaves a thing focusable and read aloud.
For text whose length is not known ahead (an error, a status), keep a place of whole lines instead: min-height: var(--ds-slot-hint) or var(--ds-slot-status).

accessibility.notes: A hidden child is out of the accessibility tree and the tab order, so only the shown one is read, as the button's or the tag's name.

slots.forms: Each form the place can take, one shown and the rest hidden.

anatomy.compositionNotes: In a button, a chip or a tag the shown form is centered; elsewhere it starts at the left.

panel.name: Panel
panel.description: A group of related parts on the page: a hairline on the page's ground.
panel.example:
Llama 3.1 8B Instruct Raw

Novita · meta-llama-128k · the top 20 candidates
constraints: Flat: no shadow and no fill. One shadow is for things that float, and panels do not.
No blur or glass.

accessibility.notes: A panel is layout; give it a heading if it is a region.

slots.header: An optional title and a tag.

anatomy.compositionNotes: Panels in a grid with --ds-space-4 between.

figure.name: Figure
figure.description: A captioned figure: a head with a number and a name, the content, a caption.
constraints: Every figure has a caption.
Head: "Fig. 1.1 · One step of the loop" in a .ds-figure-head label.
Corners signal function: this is something you read, so it stays square (--ds-radius-read).

bar.name: Bar
bar.description: A horizontal bar for a value, its number always beside it. In a row (.ds-bar-row): what it measures, the bar, the number, a hairline below.
constraints: Fill from the data layer: viridis for ordered values, or the matching gray.
Show the number too; never color alone.
The width is the value, set on the fill as a percentage.
A number that updates keeps its place: IBM Plex Mono's figures are one width, and its column fits the longest value.

accessibility.notes: The number beside it is the accessible value.

slots.what: first: what the bar measures, in mono
slots.number: last: the value, right-aligned in mono

anatomy.compositionNotes: Rows of bars in a figure, one row per value.

table.name: Table
table.description: Rows to read: small gray labels for the header, hairlines between rows.
table.example:
ModelProviderTokenizerCompletions
Llama 3.1 8B InstructNovitameta-llama-128kRaw
GPT-OSS 120BNovitagpt-oss-199kRaw
GLM 5.3Togetherglm-154kTemplated
constraints: Corners signal function: this is something you read, so it stays square (--ds-radius-read).
A table wider than a phone goes in .ds-table-wrap, which scrolls sideways so the page never does.
A value that updates keeps its column's width: IBM Plex Sans figures are one width, and a number that can gain a digit holds its widest form in a .ds-hold.

ariaRequired: on .ds-table-wrap: tabindex="0", role="region" and an aria-label, so a keyboard can reach and scroll it

anatomy.compositionNotes: Leave out the wrap only when the table is narrow at every width.

label.name: Label
label.description: Metadata in sentence case, small and gray: a figure's number, a column, a field's name.
label.example: Fig. 1.1 · One step of the loop
constraints: Short noun phrases; a middle dot separates parts.
Sentence case, like everything else; the label roles (--ds-font-label, --ds-case-label) set the face and case.

accessibility.notes: Use <label for> when it names a field.

running-head.name: Running head
running-head.description: A row of labels over a strong rule at the top of a page: the area, and n of N.
constraints: Two parts, left and right.

accessibility.notes: Plain text; the area may be a link to its first page.

topbar.name: Top bar
topbar.description: The top of every page: the mark (to aroughidea.com), the app's name (to its home), the app's areas, then its tools.
topbar.example:
A Rough Idea / App name
Guides Tools
topbar.specimenNote: The top of this page is the specimen.
constraints: The same areas on every page; the current area underlined (aria-current="true").
Never lists a page's sections; those go in "On this page".
On a phone the mark stands for the name and the areas take a row of their own.
Corners signal function: this is something you read, so it stays square (--ds-radius-read).

accessibility.notes: The areas are a <nav aria-label="Areas">; the mark link has aria-label="A Rough Idea".

anatomy.compositionNotes: Tools hold icon buttons: present, then light and dark.

mark.name: Mark
mark.description: A Rough Idea's square A, inline SVG colored from roles so it follows light and dark.
mark.example: <svg class="ds-mark" role="img" aria-label="A Rough Idea" viewBox="0 0 64 64"><rect class="ds-mark-paper" x="3" y="3" width="58" height="58" stroke-width="4"></rect><path class="ds-mark-ink" d="M14 48L32 12L50 48H42L32 28L22 48H14Z"></path><rect class="ds-mark-ink" x="28" y="31" width="8" height="17"></rect></svg>
constraints: 24 px in every top bar, linking to aroughidea.com.
An app keeps its own mark as its icon and favicon.
The full lockup (mark, bar, name in spaced capitals) only for big moments: the top of aroughidea.com, print covers, a deck's title slide.

accessibility.notes: aria-hidden inside a link labeled "A Rough Idea"; role="img" with a label when it stands alone.

rail.name: Rail
rail.description: A vertical list of links: an area's pages, or "On this page". The current item has a rule in the margin.
rail.example:
• The next-token loop
  • Temperature and sampling
  • Tokens and vocabularies
constraints: aria-current="page" for the current page; aria-current="true" for the section in view.
Pages on the left from 960 px; sections on the right from 1280 px.
The current item is semibold, so keep each entry to one line: the heavier weight must not wrap it.

accessibility.notes: Name the nav: the area, or "On this page".

seq.name: Previous and next
seq.description: The foot of a page or guide: previous and next, each naming where it goes.
seq.example: Previous← The next-token loop NextTokens and vocabularies →
constraints: rel="prev" and rel="next".
Each names its page; never "Next" alone.
The browser's back is never overridden.

note-number.name: Note number
note-number.description: A numbered circle that marks a note on a drawing.
constraints: Circles, not squares.

accessibility.notes: Number the note in the text the same way, so the circle is never the only link between them.

present-bar.name: Presentation bar
present-bar.description: Presentation mode (/v2/present.js): a page's sections as slides, with a bar of previous and next as plain arrows, the caption, n / N, full screen and Exit.
present-bar.example:
A full-sentence headline

…
present-bar.specimenNote: Press Present in this page's top bar, or Ctrl+Alt+P, to see it.

data-ds-slides.description: On the element that holds the sections.

data-ds-present.description: On the button that starts it.

data-ds-present-prev.description: A page to continue to before the first slide.

constraints: Each <section> directly inside data-ds-slides is one slide; its <h2> is the headline, a full sentence.
Start with the button, Ctrl+Alt+P or ?mode=presentation.
Arrows are plain, never boxed.
A slide that does not fit scrolls; a real deck splits it.
The bar holds still from slide to slide: on a phone the caption keeps two lines (--ds-slot-caption).

accessibility.notes: Everything outside the slides is made inert while presenting.

anatomy.compositionNotes: Built by present.js; do not write it by hand.

lockup.name: Lockup
lockup.description: The full lockup: the mark, a bar and the name in spaced Archivo capitals, the only capitals in the system. Side by side, or stacked for the centered layout.
lockup.example: A Rough Idea

variantGuidance.side by side: class="ds-lockup": mark, bar, name in a row.
variantGuidance.stacked: class="ds-lockup ds-lockup--stacked": mark above name, no bar (it only reads side by side). Use it in the centered layout.

constraints: Only for big moments: the top of aroughidea.com, a print cover, a deck's title slide. Top bars use the mark and the name (topbar, .ds-brand).
One lockup per page.
The name in capitals here and nowhere else.

accessibility.element: <div class="ds-lockup" role="img" aria-label="A Rough Idea">, or an <h1> when it is the page's title
accessibility.notes: The mark inside is aria-hidden; the label or heading carries the name.

slots.name: A Rough Idea
slots.words: optional <span class="ds-lockup-words"> holding the name and a .ds-label beneath it

anatomy.compositionNotes: Stacked inside .ds-centered; side by side elsewhere.

centered-layout.name: Centered layout
centered-layout.description: Everything centered on the reading column: for a page with one thing to say, such as a home page, a title slide or an exhibit's opening screen. aroughidea.com uses it.
centered-layout.example:
A Rough Idea

A consultancy operating at the intersection of systems design and machine behavior.
constraints: Put .ds-centered on the element that holds the page's content, one column at the reading measure.
Use the stacked lockup in it, never the side-by-side one.
Keep to short lines: running text longer than about three lines stays left-aligned.
A figure inside takes the column's full width; its drawing and caption center.

accessibility.notes: Centering changes nothing for a screen reader; keep the reading order the visual order.

anatomy.compositionNotes: One column at --ds-measure; gaps from the spacing scale.
